meta.titre: Reading Comprehension: finding, inferring and answering from the text
meta.sous_theme: Answering literal, inferential and own-words questions on a passage

source.epreuve_titre: GCE A/L English Language past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A trader in Bamenda reads a contract line by line before she signs, because one misunderstood word can cost her a whole season's profit. A comprehension passage deserves the same care. The examiner has built questions on what the text says, on what it suggests and on how the writer feels, and your marks come from reading with that much attention. At Advanced Level the questions go beyond finding facts: they ask you to infer, to judge tone and to explain in your own words. This course gives one method that works for multiple-choice items and for written answers on prose and poetry.

items: A paragraph develops one main idea, which is often announced in its first or last sentence.
A synonym is a word with nearly the same meaning as another word.
Prose is ordinary writing in sentences; a poem is arranged in lines and often in stanzas.

sections.titre: Reading a passage and answering by level of question
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Three levels of meaning

Every question tests one of three levels.

| Level | What it asks | How to answer |
|---|---|---|
| Literal | What the text states directly | Find the sentence, then restate it |
| Inferential | What the text suggests without stating it | Join the clues and explain your conclusion |
| Evaluative | The writer's attitude, tone or purpose, or the effect of a device | Name the feeling or purpose, then support it with a detail from the text |

### Method before you answer

1. Read the title and the questions first, so that you know what to look for.
2. Read the passage once without stopping, then again with a pencil, marking evidence for each question.
3. Treat a line reference (such as L.5) as a starting point only. Read the sentences before and after it, because context can change a meaning.
4. Answer in the order of the questions. The evidence usually follows the order of the passage.

### Multiple-choice items

Choose the option that the passage supports, not the one that is true in general or merely sounds clever. Reject an option that contradicts the text, one that goes beyond it by adding a claim the writer never makes, and one that repeats a word from the text but changes its meaning. When an item is a sentence to complete, your choice must make a complete and grammatical sentence.

### Written answers

- Answer the exact question: "why" needs a reason, "how" needs a method, "what" needs a fact.
- Write a full sentence that carries the key words of the question. A fragment may leave the examiner guessing what you mean.
- When the question says "in your own words", do not copy the sentence from the text. Keep only names and technical terms that cannot be replaced.
- Stop when the question is answered. A short, exact answer is better than a long one with a wrong detail in it.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question says suggest, imply, attitude, tone or feel
variantes.contenu_markdown: Find the clue words (adjectives, verbs, images) and name the feeling precisely: sympathetic, critical, ironic, nostalgic, admiring. Words such as "good" or "bad" are too vague. Then show the evidence. A reliable pattern is: *The writer feels ___ because the words "___" suggest ___.*

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question says in your own words, explain or rephrase
variantes.contenu_markdown: Replace each key word by a synonym or a short explanation, and change the sentence structure if you can, but keep the meaning exactly. Do not add opinions or details. Changing only one word is not a paraphrase.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the passage is a poem and the question asks for its message or the speaker's feelings
variantes.contenu_markdown: Identify the speaker, the situation and any change of feeling from stanza to stanza. State the message in one clear sentence beginning "The poem suggests that...", then support it with one or two images or word choices and explain what each contributes. Several readings can be accepted if the text supports them.

sections.enonce_markdown:
Read the passage and answer the questions.

> The village school had no running water. Because they had to walk two kilometres to the stream every morning, many pupils reached class late and tired. When the council failed to answer their letters, the parents' association collected a small sum from every household and paid a mechanic to repair the old borehole. Within a month the pump was working again and the classrooms were full. The headmaster later admitted that he had been wrong to wait for outside help.

(a) Why did many pupils arrive late?

(b) What does the parents' decision to collect money show about their attitude?

(c) Explain in your own words what the headmaster admitted.

(d) The passage mainly shows that (A) councils always ignore letters, (B) a community can solve its own problem, (C) boreholes are expensive to repair, (D) headmasters often make mistakes.

etapes.justification: The type of question tells you what kind of evidence to look for and how to word the answer.
etapes.resultat_markdown: (a) literal; (b) inferential; (c) own words; (d) main idea, multiple choice.

etapes.action: Read the passage and mark the evidence for each question.
etapes.justification: Marking evidence stops you from answering from general knowledge instead of from the text.
etapes.resultat_markdown: (a) "walk two kilometres to the stream every morning"; (b) "failed to answer" then "collected a small sum"; (c) the last sentence; (d) the whole passage.

etapes.action: Answer the literal question with a full sentence and the reason.
etapes.justification: A "why" question needs a cause, stated clearly and in a complete sentence.
etapes.resultat_markdown: (a) Many pupils arrived late because the school had no running water, so they had to walk two kilometres to the stream every morning.

etapes.action: Answer the inferential question by joining two clues.
etapes.justification: The attitude is never stated. It is shown by what the parents did after the council failed to answer.
etapes.resultat_markdown: (b) The parents were practical and self-reliant: they did not wait for the council, but paid for the repair themselves.

etapes.action: Rewrite the last sentence in your own words.
etapes.justification: Each key expression is replaced: "admitted" becomes "accepted", "wait for outside help" becomes "hope that someone else would solve the problem".
etapes.resultat_markdown: (c) He accepted that it had been a mistake to hope that someone from outside the school would solve the problem.

etapes.action: Test each option of the multiple-choice item against the text.
etapes.justification: "Always" in (A) goes beyond the text, which mentions only one council. (C) is not discussed. (D) is only a detail, not the main idea.
etapes.resultat_markdown: (d) **(B)**: the parents repaired the borehole themselves and the school improved.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The model answers use a full sentence for each written question, rely on evidence from the passage, avoid copying in (c) and eliminate three options in (d) by naming what is wrong with each.

items.erreur_markdown: In an own-words question, the pupil copies: *"The headmaster later admitted that he had been wrong to wait for outside help."*
items.pourquoi_faux: The sentence is taken directly from the text, which shows no understanding of it.
items.correction_markdown: *He recognised that it had been a mistake to expect someone from outside to solve the problem.*

items.erreur_markdown: In a multiple-choice item the pupil picks "Education is the key to success" because it is true in general, although the passage does not say it.
items.pourquoi_faux: The item asks what the passage supports, not what is true in the world.
items.correction_markdown: Check each option against the lines of the passage and choose the one the writer actually supports.

items.erreur_markdown: "The tone of the writer is good."
items.pourquoi_faux: "Good" does not name a feeling. It does not tell the examiner whether the writer is admiring, critical or amused.
items.correction_markdown: *The tone is admiring, because the writer praises the parents for acting without waiting.*

items.erreur_markdown: Question: "Why were the pupils tired?" Answer: "The pupils were tired and late."
items.pourquoi_faux: The answer repeats the facts of the passage and gives no reason.
items.correction_markdown: *The pupils were tired because they had to walk two kilometres to the stream every morning.*

items.erreur_markdown: The pupil reads only the line given in the question and misses a word such as *not* or *but* in the next line.
items.pourquoi_faux: A single line can say the opposite of the sentence that completes it.
items.correction_markdown: Read the sentences before and after the line reference, then answer.

items.enonce_markdown:
Read the passage.

> Mireille's mother sold tomatoes at the roadside so that her daughter could finish secondary school. Every evening Mireille helped her count the unsold tomatoes, then studied by the light of a small lamp. When the examination results arrived, she did not run home to celebrate. She walked slowly to the roadside, stood beside her mother and held out the paper without a word.

(a) How did Mireille's mother support her daughter's education?

(b) When did Mireille study?
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **She sold tomatoes at the roadside to earn the money for her daughter's schooling.** Award a mark for the activity and a mark for the purpose (the daughter's schooling).

(b) **In the evening, by the light of a small lamp**, after she had helped to count the unsold tomatoes.

items.enonce_markdown:
Use the passage about Mireille.

(a) What does Mireille's behaviour in the last sentence suggest about her feelings towards her mother?

(b) Explain in your own words how Mireille's mother made it possible for her to complete her schooling.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **She felt gratitude and respect for her mother, and she wanted to share the success with her.** She does not run home alone but goes to her mother and gives her the paper silently, which suggests that her emotion is too strong for words. Award a mark for the feeling and a mark for the evidence.

(b) **Her mother earned money by selling vegetables beside the road, and this paid for her daughter to stay at school until she finished.** The answer must not copy the phrase "sold tomatoes at the roadside".

items.enonce_markdown:
Read the poem.

> The old well at the edge of the village
> still holds the sky in its dark water.
> Children no longer come with buckets;
> the pipe in the square has taught them
> to forget the rope, the song, the waiting.
> Only the moss remembers the hands.

(a) Write a short paragraph explaining what the poem suggests about change in the village. Support your answer from the poem.

(b) Describe the tone of the poem and give two pieces of evidence.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **The poem suggests that progress has brought convenience but has also taken away shared habits and human contact.** The pipe in the square has replaced the well, so children "no longer come with buckets" and have "forgotten the rope, the song, the waiting". These words show that fetching water was a social experience with songs and waiting together, and not only a chore. The last line, in which only the moss "remembers the hands", suggests that nobody else remembers the people who used the well. Award a mark for a clear statement of the idea, a mark for each of two relevant pieces of evidence, and a mark for explaining what the evidence shows.

(b) **The tone is nostalgic and gently regretful.** Evidence: "no longer" and "forget" speak of loss; the well still "holds the sky", an image of quiet beauty that is now unused; and the moss, given the human ability to remember, is the only witness left (personification). Accept another precise tone word (for example wistful) when it is supported by evidence.

items_markdown: Identify the level of each question first: literal (stated), inferential (suggested) or evaluative (attitude, tone, effect).
Support every answer with evidence from the text and read around a line reference before you answer.
In multiple-choice items, choose what the passage supports and reject options that go beyond it or change a word's meaning.
Use your own words when asked, keep a complete sentence that carries the key words of the question, and give a reason for every "why".
For tone and message questions, name the feeling or idea precisely and prove it with words from the text.
